question_text: State the Pythagoras theorem.
easy_answer: In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.

question_text: State the converse of Pythagoras theorem.
hint: It helps identify a right triangle from side lengths.
easy_answer: If the square of the longest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides, the triangle is right-angled opposite the longest side.

question_text: Explain how the converse of Pythagoras theorem can be used in construction work.
hint: It can check whether an angle is 90°.
easy_answer: Measure three sides. If a²+b²=c² for the longest side c, the included angle opposite c is a right angle.
